Draw the W of Cassiopeia on the land in light. Then its five bright stars fall one by one, dimmest first, each crater as wide as its star is bright, each leaving a glowing star core standing in it. The brightest, Schedar, comes last, and veins of starlight run along the W between the craters. Power widens it all; Damage is what the blasts do (infinity erases what stands in a crater).
